purpose: After eliminating all nonterminal rank-2 bulk, repeatedly absorb every 3-clause interaction already implied by the terminal 2-CNF closure. The result is an implication-primitive rank-3 core in which no remaining 3-clause can be shortened or deleted using any unary/binary consequence of the current bijunctive layer.
input: K(F)=H AND F3 from v3.7, where H is a satisfiable 2-CNF over terminal variables and F3 is the set of genuine 3-clauses.

rules.name: FORCED_TRUE
rules.condition: H entails literal a (equivalently NOT a reaches a in the implication graph).

rules.name: FORCED_FALSE
rules.condition: H entails NOT a (equivalently a reaches NOT a).
rules.action: Delete a from every 3-clause containing it. A resulting 2-clause is moved into H.

rules.name: IMPLIED_DOMINATION
rules.condition: A 3-clause contains distinct literals a,b,c and H entails a -> b.
rules.action: Replace (a OR b OR c) by (b OR c) and move the binary clause into H. Under H the two formulas are equivalent.

rules.name: ENTAILED_SUBCLAUSE
rules.condition: For two literals a,b of a 3-clause, H entails (a OR b), equivalently NOT a -> b in the implication closure.

algorithm.loop: Apply a rule, rebuild/close the implication graph of H, reject if H becomes inconsistent, and continue until no rule applies.
algorithm.progress: Every non-rejection rule either removes a 3-clause or replaces one by a 2-clause. Hence the number of 3-clauses strictly decreases on every substantive step; there are at most k such steps after duplicate/tautology cleanup.
algorithm.runtime: Polynomial. A simple implementation may recompute SCC/reachability after each step; incremental implication maintenance is optional and not required for the theorem.

theorem.name: IMPLICATION_PRIMITIVE_RANK3_NORMAL_FORM
theorem.statement: The procedure preserves satisfiability and polynomial witness reconstruction. At termination, for every remaining 3-clause (a OR b OR c): no literal is forced by H; no literal is forced false by H; no literal implies another literal in the same clause; and H entails no binary subclause formed by two of its literals.
proof: FORCED_TRUE and FORCED_FALSE are ordinary substitution by consequences of H.
If H entails a -> b, then under H any model of (a OR b OR c) with b=false and c=false cannot use a=true, because a would force b. Thus (a OR b OR c) is equivalent under H to (b OR c).
If H entails (a OR b), then H already satisfies (a OR b OR c), so the 3-clause is redundant.
Every added binary clause is logically equivalent to the removed 3-clause relative to the previous H, so iterating closure preserves the total model set projected to the surviving variables.
Termination properties follow because otherwise one of the rules would still apply.

interpretation.positive: The hard frontier can be assumed to contain only 3-clauses that are genuinely new relative to every unary/binary implication already available. Rank-3 atoms that merely restate rank-2 information are removed exactly.
interpretation.not_a_solver: For a pure arbitrary 3-CNF with empty H, the normal form may do nothing. Thus this is a strict preprocessing theorem, not universal tractability.
interpretation.anti_loop: Do not count a 3-clause as a hard atom until it survives this implication-primitive reduction.

next_target.name: E8_PRIMITIVE_RANK3_GLOBAL_HYPERIMPLICATION_CONTRACTION_V3_9
next_target.directive: Attack only implication-primitive 3-clauses. Each such clause contributes the genuinely ternary rule that if two literals are false the third must be true. Seek a polynomial closure/contraction for these pair-antecedent hyperimplications that does not enumerate pairs/subsets exponentially and that strictly reduces the number of primitive rank-3 atoms or returns an exact global UNSAT certificate.
